# OmicOS OSS

A research application built on open-source Harness: native conversations, Agents,
approvals and plu

gins, with persistent Python/R, data, notebooks, figures, project
memory, scientific workflows and a
n optional OmicOS cloud subscription store.

**Development preview (0.3.0).** This branch implements the first scientific and
commerce vertical s

lice. It does not yet provide all OmicOS Core capabilities.
See implementation status and the
comple

te migration design. No private Core binary is
required by the OSS backend; the old Core adapter rem

design. No private Core binary is
required by the OSS backend; the old Core adapter remains opt-in.
## Run the OmicOS application

The primary UI is the complete Harness application, restyled and composed as OmicOS:
a narrow functi

on rail, the native workspace/session browser, central conversations,
and dockable scientific side t

abs. Data, Notebook, Figures, Memory, Pipelines,
Methods/Evidence, Runtime and Store open inside the

application. The conversation's
OmicOS view also contains these project tools directly; no iframe o

r separate dashboard
is needed. The stock Agent, streaming, model selection, approval, settings and

plugin
mechanisms remain available. The deployment default is OmicOS Scientist; a user's
chosen defa
ult in native Settings takes precedence.

The command installs the pinned published Harness engine into an isolated OmicOS
profile and opens i

ts actual root application on loopback. Its default home is
`~/.omicos-oss/application`; `--home`, `

--python`, `--rscript`, `--port`, `--locale en|zh`
and `--no-open` are available. Initial engine ins

tallation requires npm registry access.
Models are configured through native settings; the launcher

does not synthesize a key
or copy model/cloud credentials from the environment. OmicOS cloud account

s and
subscriptions are managed separately in the Store.

The selected directory is the initial working directory, not a global override of
other conversation

s: scientific tools and docked panes follow each native Session's
workspace. Main scientific pages a

lso expose their project selector. Default language
and Scientist selection are contributed by a pri

vate application defaults bundle,
below the native user profile patch. Native Settings can change th

em
and retain those choices across restart; `--locale` sets the deployment default.
The generated sc

ientific-runtime overlay is separate from user profile patches and
model settings. An exclusive prof

ile lease rejects duplicate launch before changing its configuration;
graceful shutdown releases the

lease. Native approvals still govern Agent actions,
and data reads never start an analysis or purch

s`,
`pnpm run build:check`, and

g its pinned pnpm 11.28.5.

## Legacy Core compatibility

Set `backend: core` to use the original delegated Core Agent tools. Install the
Core package separat

ely if desired; it is no longer downloaded as an OSS package
dependency. The legacy adapter may atta

ch to/start Core according to its config.
It has a separate Core-managed cloud identity; OSS login d

oes not migrate it.
Read legacy Core instructions for the existing tool/command
surface. This compat
ibility backend is not the standalone open-source path.
## Capability discovery

Run `omicos-oss --version` to inspect the installed version without opening a project.
The owner-aut

henticated `GET /omicos/oss/api/capabilities` describes the runtime
version, supported scientific pr

otocol and implemented/optional/unverified features.
It never starts interpreters or contacts cloud.

Send `x-omicos-protocol: 1` to API
requests; an unsupported explicit version returns HTTP 426 befor

e dispatch. Discovery
remains accessible after owner authentication even with a mismatched header. E

xisting
clients without the header retain protocol-1 behavior. The workbench footer and
`omicos_runt
ime_capabilities` Agent tool expose the same contract.

The pinned Harness rc.3 adapter has native unload/remount and WebServer-replacement
coverage, includ

ing actual worker ownership, interrupted receipts and SSE cleanup.
Concurrent startup requests share

one handler/CSRF generation; retired routes fail
before dispatch. Full plugin unload restarts an ar

bitrary Python namespace cold;
carrier-only replacement preserves it. See [lifecycle evidence and re

maining
platform limits](docs/adr/0022-harness-generation-lifecycle.md).

Retained Scientist preset bindings also follow the current Host provider after
remount: the next con

text prepares authorized MCP tools and refreshes the public
prompt assembly, while current memory st

ays literal and approvals remain required.
Cold transcript reads do not start transports. See [retai

ned-scope evidence and
remaining live-streaming limits](docs/adr/0023-retained-scientist-context.md)

ed-scope evidence and
remaining live-streaming limits](docs/adr/0023-retained-scientist-context.md).

Scientist chat now streams visible text through the same Harness controller, with
partial reconnect

baselines and committed history. Closing the window stops only
its observer; explicit Stop retains t

he existing cancel path. Reasoning, tool
arguments and injected context are not relayed to this chat

surface. Text windows
are bounded and full history remains Harness-owned. See [stream protocol, lim

its
and verification](docs/adr/0024-fixed-conversation-stream.md).
